man-shot-dead-on-midtown-subway-platform.title: Man Shot Dead on Midtown Subway Platform; Masked Gunman Sought
man-shot-dead-on-midtown-subway-platform.dek: A 26-year-old Bronx man was shot and killed during an argument at the 53rd Street-Seventh Avenue station. Police are still looking for the suspect.
body: Saturday, just before 12:30 p.m. The 53rd Street-Seventh Avenue subway station in Midtown Manhattan. A 26-year-old Bronx man was shot and killed during an argument with another man, FOX 5 NY reported. Police said the attack was not random.

Officials said the argument started on the northbound platform, according to FOX 5. It continued as the two men boarded a subway car. It started again after they stepped back onto the platform. Then the suspect drew a gun and shot the man in the chest.
First responders took the man to a hospital. He was pronounced dead there, FOX 5 reported.

The NYPD released surveillance images of the suspect, according to FOX 5. He wore a red tracksuit, a black vest, a black face mask and a black backpack. His name is not known. Neither is where he is now.
The search for him goes on. Anyone with information can call NYPD Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS, or 1-888-57-PISTA for Spanish.

queens-officers-revive-infant-in-frantic.title: Two NYPD Officers Revive Infant With CPR in Astoria
queens-officers-revive-infant-in-frantic.dek: Officers Douglas Zimmerman and Jesutofunmi Aregbesola got a 1-month-old boy breathing again in under two minutes after a call in Queens, NY1 reported.
body: Astoria, Queens. A call came in about an infant who was not breathing and had no pulse. Two NYPD officers responded. They are now being credited with saving the life of the 1-month-old boy, according to NY1.

The officers are Douglas Zimmerman and Jesutofunmi Aregbesola. Each has been on the job about two years, the outlet reported. They worked together to revive the baby. Zimmerman started the rescue effort. Aregbesola then took over CPR. Their body-worn cameras recorded it.

Less than two minutes after the officers arrived, the infant was breathing again, NY1 reported. Aregbesola told the outlet he saw the baby's eyes open and his color come back. He said his academy training took over in the moment.
Zimmerman said seconds matter when helping a child that young, according to the report.
About two weeks after the call, the officers said they had heard from the family. The baby was doing well, NY1 reported. The outlet did not say exactly when the rescue took place.

queens-father-sues-nypd-says-officers-st.title: Queens Father Sues NYPD, Alleging Officers Struck Moped Carrying His Teenage Son
queens-father-sues-nypd-says-officers-st.dek: A federal lawsuit says a marked police vehicle crossed a double yellow line in Corona and swerved into a moped carrying a 14-year-old passenger.
body: A Queens father has filed a federal lawsuit in Brooklyn. It accuses NYPD officers of deliberately steering a marked police vehicle into a moped carrying his 14-year-old son in Corona, Hoodline reported, citing the New York Daily News.

The crash happened near 101st Street and Northern Boulevard, according to the suit. That evening, officers from the 115th Precinct and the Community Response Team were targeting a group of mopeds in a joint operation, the lawsuit says. The teen was a passenger in that group. The suit alleges a police car came from the opposite direction with its lights and sirens off. It says the car crossed the double yellow line and swerved into the moped's path.

The teen was knocked unconscious, according to the suit. He suffered a fractured femur and a head bruise. His father said the boy was handcuffed while injured. He said officers later told him his son would not be charged. The handcuffs came off after a CT scan, the lawsuit says.

The family's attorney is Jon Norinsberg. He alleges the NYPD has an unwritten practice of using police vehicles to block or strike two-wheeled vehicles. The department's Patrol Guide prohibits that. The allegations have not been proven in court.

An NYPD spokesperson declined to say what officers were responding to. The spokesperson also declined to say whether anyone was arrested, and said an internal investigation is ongoing. The city Law Department declined to comment, according to the report. In January 2025, Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch tightened the department's vehicle pursuit policy.

woman-68-slashed-in-sheepshead-bay-subwa.title: Woman, 68, Slashed in Sheepshead Bay Subway Door Dispute
woman-68-slashed-in-sheepshead-bay-subwa.dek: A man who had propped open an emergency exit door allegedly cut a 68-year-old woman's face with a knife. A person of interest was taken into custody.
body: Saturday morning. The Sheepshead Bay B/Q subway station. A 68-year-old woman was slashed in the face after a dispute with a man who had propped open an emergency exit door, Hoodline reported.
The dispute started at about 9 a.m., according to Hoodline. The man allegedly held a knife to the woman's face and cut her. Then he ran onto the platform and got on a southbound Q train.

NYPD Transit officers took a 70-year-old man into custody at the station, Hoodline reported. He was described as a person of interest. Charges were pending as of the report. The woman refused medical attention at the scene.

People sometimes prop open the exit-only doors to ask riders for money, according to the New York Post, as cited by Hoodline. NYPD data cited by the Post showed felony assault complaints in the transit system rose 12% this year as of Oct. 13. They went from 470 to 525.
A stabbing outside a lounge on Avenue U a week earlier was unrelated, Hoodline reported. The man in custody has not been charged. He is presumed innocent.

bronx-man-68-accused-of-shooting-girlfri.title: Bronx Man, 68, Accused of Shooting Girlfriend and Another Man
bronx-man-68-accused-of-shooting-girlfri.dek: A 70-year-old woman and a 60-year-old man were seriously wounded in a ninth-floor apartment on Third Avenue in the Bronx on Oct. 17. A suspect was arrested, Hoy reported.
body: Saturday, Oct. 17, shortly before 9:30 p.m. A ninth-floor apartment at 3970 Third Avenue, at 173rd Street, in the Bronx. A woman and a man were shot, according to the newspaper Hoy, citing authorities. A 68-year-old man has been arrested and charged with attempted murder.
Hoy identified the suspect as Kenneth Morgan. He allegedly shot his 70-year-old girlfriend. He allegedly also shot a 60-year-old man who was with her.

The woman was wounded in the abdomen, according to the report. The man suffered several gunshot wounds to the chest. Both were taken to a hospital in serious condition. Authorities did not release their names.
The suspect barricaded himself inside an apartment before he was taken into custody, Hoy reported. Investigators recovered several shell casings in the building's hallway, the newspaper said.

Morgan faces charges of attempted murder, assault, criminal possession of a weapon and reckless endangerment, according to the report. The charges are accusations. He is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

man-54-wounded-in-shooting-outside-maria.title: Man, 54, Wounded in Shooting Outside Maria Hernandez Park
man-54-wounded-in-shooting-outside-maria.dek: A 54-year-old man was shot in the leg in front of 202 Starr Street in Bushwick. Police are looking for three people.
body: Oct. 8, afternoon. In front of 202 Starr Street in Bushwick. A 54-year-old man was shot in the leg, Hoodline reported.

Uniformed NYPD officers were in nearby Maria Hernandez Park on an unrelated matter. They heard the shots and reached the man within moments, according to a Grime Square report cited by Hoodline. He was taken to a hospital. He was listed in stable condition.

Police are looking for three unidentified people wanted for assault, according to an NYPD Crime Stoppers post. Police said one person brought a gun. A second displayed it and fired it. A third took the weapon. All three ran south on foot along Knickerbocker Avenue, Hoodline reported.

The 83rd Precinct covers Bushwick. Total crime there is up 15% year over year through October, according to Grime Square. Felony assaults are up 35.2%. Citywide, officials announced record-low shootings for the first nine months of the year.
No arrests had been made as of mid-October, according to Grime Square. Anyone with information can contact Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS.

dyker-heights-mother-and-two-children-re.title: Dyker Heights Mother and Two Children Reported Missing
dyker-heights-mother-and-two-children-re.dek: The NYPD is asking for help finding a 40-year-old woman who left her home with her two young children on Oct. 9.
body: A 40-year-old Dyker Heights woman and her two children have been missing for more than a week. The children are 5 and 9. The NYPD is asking the public for help finding them, Hoodline reported.
Oct. 9, about 10:10 a.m. The woman left the family's home with both children after an argument with her husband, according to police cited by the New York Daily News, as reported by Hoodline.

Police describe the woman as about 5 feet 8 inches tall and 135 pounds. She has shoulder-length red hair and blue eyes, Hoodline reported. No description of the children was given. The 68th Precinct patrols Dyker Heights.

Hoodline did not report whether an AMBER Alert had been issued. Under New York's AMBER plan, an alert requires reasonable cause to believe a child was abducted or is in imminent danger, according to Hoodline. Otherwise, agencies can request a Missing Child Alert through the state's Missing Persons Clearinghouse.
As of the report, the three had not been found. Anyone with information is asked to contact NYPD Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

nypd-hunts-two-suspects-in-lower-manhatt.title: NYPD Seeks Two Suspects in Lower Manhattan Robbery Pattern
nypd-hunts-two-suspects-in-lower-manhatt.dek: Crime Stoppers released images of two people wanted in connection with a string of robberies in the 5th Precinct.
body: NYPD Crime Stoppers is asking the public to help identify two people. They are wanted in connection with a pattern of robberies in Lower Manhattan's 5th Precinct, Hoodline reported.
Friday, Oct. 16, at night. The unit posted images of the pair on X, according to Hoodline. The 5th Precinct covers southeastern Manhattan. That includes Chinatown, Little Italy and the Bowery.

The NYPD has not said when or where the robberies happened, Hoodline reported. It has not said what was taken or whether anyone was hurt. Police have not released names, ages or descriptions of the two people sought.

At an Oct. 6 briefing, the department said robberies were down 12% citywide this year, according to Hoodline. That is about 1,400 fewer complaints than at the same point in 2025. Police did not say whether the 5th Precinct follows that trend. Hoodline noted other robbery patterns reported in the Bronx and Manhattan this year. It said none had been linked to this case.
The two suspects have not been identified. Crime Stoppers offers up to $3,500 for anonymous information leading to an arrest and indictment. Tips can be called in to 1-800-577-TIPS.

astoria-man-42-shot-in-leg-on-steinway-s.title: Astoria Man, 42, Shot in Leg on Steinway Street
astoria-man-42-shot-in-leg-on-steinway-s.dek: A gunman opened fire near Steinway Street and 31st Avenue early Saturday. Witnesses reported a white SUV driving away.
body: Saturday, Oct. 17, about 6:36 a.m. Steinway Street near 31st Avenue in Astoria. A 42-year-old man was shot in the left leg near a sidewalk bench, Hoodline reported.
The gunman fled, according to Hoodline. Witnesses told investigators they saw a white SUV driving away. No description of a suspect was released.

Responding officers drove the man to Elmhurst Hospital in their patrol car. They did not wait for an ambulance, the New York Daily News reported, as cited by Hoodline. Police said he was expected to survive.

Detectives interviewed witnesses at the scene, according to Hoodline. They were canvassing for surveillance footage of the gunman or the SUV. Neighbors suggested a link to a nearby party venue. Police have not confirmed that. Police have not disclosed a motive.
There were no arrests as of Saturday. Police have not pointed to any connection to a fatal shooting on Steinway Street in September, Hoodline reported.

vacate-order-issued-after-crash-into-how.title: Vacate Order Issued After SUV Crashes Into Howard Beach Pizzeria
vacate-order-issued-after-crash-into-how.dek: City inspectors ordered New Park Pizzeria's building vacated after a BMW SUV hit its dining area Thursday. Two people were hurt, the FDNY said.
body: Thursday afternoon. Cross Bay Boulevard in Howard Beach, Queens. An SUV crashed into New Park Pizzeria. City inspectors then issued a full vacate order for the building, NY1 reported.

The BMW SUV struck a part of the building used for dining shortly after 1 p.m. on Oct. 15, according to the FDNY. Two people were injured: the driver and a person inside the restaurant. Both were taken to Brookdale University Hospital Medical Center. Their injuries were not life-threatening, the FDNY said.

The NYPD's Emergency Service Unit responded Thursday afternoon to remove the vehicle, according to NY1. By Friday morning, vacate orders were posted on the restaurant's door. They warned people not to enter. Green scaffolding had gone up around the damaged section of the building.
The cause of the crash was not reported. NY1 said it had contacted the Department of Buildings for comment.
In a social media post, the pizzeria said it is working to reopen as quickly as possible.

five-men-sought-after-man-stabbed-outsid.title: Five Men Sought After Man Stabbed Outside University Avenue Building
five-men-sought-after-man-stabbed-outsid.dek: A 35-year-old man was stabbed in the back and cut on the hand outside 2274 University Ave. in the Bronx. He is expected to recover.
body: Thursday, late at night. Outside a residential building in University Heights, the Bronx. A 35-year-old man was stabbed. Police are looking for at least five men, Hoodline reported, citing police sources.

The attack happened in front of 2274 University Avenue, according to Hoodline. Officers found the man with a stab wound to his back and a cut to his left hand, News12 Bronx reported, as cited by Hoodline.
EMS took the man to St. Barnabas Hospital. He is expected to recover, according to Hoodline.

Police sources said they are searching for at least five men believed to be connected to the attack. What led to the stabbing has not been disclosed. No descriptions of the men were released, Hoodline reported.

No arrests have been made. The investigation is ongoing. Anyone with information can call Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS. The program offers rewards of up to $3,500 for tips leading to an arrest and indictment, according to Hoodline.

south-richmond-hill-mother-charged-with-.title: South Richmond Hill Mother Charged With Murder in Death of Daughter, 5
south-richmond-hill-mother-charged-with-.dek: A 32-year-old woman is held without bail, charged in the death of her kindergarten-age daughter at their Queens home.
body: A 32-year-old South Richmond Hill woman has been charged with murder in the death of her 5-year-old daughter. She is being held without bail, QNS reported, citing the Queens District Attorney's Office.

Oct. 14, shortly before 7 p.m. A 911 call reported an assault at the family's home on 110th Street. Officers from the 102nd Precinct responded, according to QNS. The girl was taken to Jamaica Hospital Medical Center. She was pronounced dead there.

The next day the woman was taken into custody as a person of interest. She was charged at Jamaica Hospital, where she was undergoing a psychiatric evaluation, QNS reported. The criminal complaint cites witness information and statements attributed to her. It also cites an autopsy finding that QNS said was consistent with asphyxia.

She was arraigned Friday before Queens Criminal Court Judge Jennifer Saint-Preux. She did not enter a plea, according to QNS. She is due back in court Oct. 20. A relative told reporters she had psychological issues, had recently been hospitalized and had stopped taking her medication.
The charges are allegations. The woman is presumed innocent. The case is ongoing.

new-charges-filed-in-fit-students-fentan.title: New Charges Filed in Fentanyl Death of FIT Student
new-charges-filed-in-fit-students-fentan.dek: Federal authorities added charges against a 19-year-old accused of giving two women fentanyl in a Fashion Institute of Technology dorm in March, NY1 reported.
body: A 19-year-old man accused in the fentanyl death of a Fashion Institute of Technology student faces new charges. They include drug distribution with intent to commit rape, according to NY1, which cited prosecutors.

March 2026. A dorm room at the Manhattan college. Prosecutors allege Moises Freire gave two women fentanyl there and told them it was cocaine, NY1 reported. They allege he urged them to take it and took none himself. Both women quickly lost consciousness, according to the allegations.

Prosecutors also allege Freire sexually assaulted one of the women. They allege he waited about 45 minutes before seeking help, the outlet said. Investigators say he falsely told campus security the women had been drinking and passed out. Security officers gave Narcan. One woman survived. The other never regained consciousness and later died.

Freire and his alleged supplier, Brian Peralta Cabrera, also face drug conspiracy charges, according to the report. Christopher Roberts is special agent in charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration's New York office. He said Freire had texted the supplier that the drug was poison, NY1 reported.

FIT told students in an email that it has strengthened safety protocols and training since the death, the outlet said. It is adding security. NY1 did not report court dates or pleas. The charges are accusations. Both men are presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

lawyers-say-ice-officer-fired-into-new-y.title: Lawyers Say ICE Officer Fired Into New Yorker's Car Without Identifying Himself
lawyers-say-ice-officer-fired-into-new-y.dek: Attorneys for a 28-year-old man shot by an immigration officer in Marble Hill on Oct. 8 dispute the federal account that he drove at officers.
body: Oct. 8. A 28-year-old man was wounded by a federal immigration officer. His lawyers say the officer came up to his car without identifying himself, smashed a window and fired several shots. One struck the man in the neck, the Associated Press reported in a story published by NY1.

Legal Aid Society attorneys filed a petition in Brooklyn federal court seeking his release. In it, they said the man, who is from the Dominican Republic, had picked up his young son from school. He was stopped near a fire hydrant looking for parking when masked, armed men approached. The son was in the back seat, the lawyers said.

Department of Homeland Security officials tell it differently. They say officers fired only after the man drove into two government vehicles and accelerated toward other officers, and that they feared for their lives. A senior ICE official said the man had refused orders to get out of the car. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said officers did not know a child was in the vehicle. DHS said the incident is under investigation.

NYPD security footage was released last week, according to the AP. It shows a man with a gun drawn striking the driver's window until it shatters. Then the car pulls away. The footage does not show the shooting. The car later came to rest against a concrete barrier. The man was taken to a hospital.

He is still detained at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn. He has not had surgery to remove the bullet, his lawyers said. The Federal Bureau of Prisons declined to discuss his care. It said it does not deny necessary treatment.

woman-sought-in-slashing-at-145th-street.title: Woman Sought in Slashing at 145th Street Subway Station
woman-sought-in-slashing-at-145th-street.dek: Transit detectives released images of a woman accused of cutting a 21-year-old woman's arm during an argument in Harlem.
body: Sept. 11, about 8 p.m. The mezzanine of the 145th Street station on the 2 line in Harlem. A 21-year-old woman's arm was slashed during an argument. Transit detectives are searching for the woman who did it, amNY reported, citing the NYPD.

Police said the suspect confronted the victim and started a verbal dispute, according to amNY. The reason was not disclosed. It turned into a physical fight. The suspect pulled out a sharp object and cut the victim's arm.
EMS took the victim to Mount Sinai Hospital in stable condition, amNY reported. The suspect fled on foot. Police do not know which way she went.

Police described the suspect as a woman in a black shirt, black pants and black sneakers, carrying a black bag. The NYPD released images of her Wednesday night, according to amNY. The case was reported to the 32nd Precinct and Transit District 3.
She was still at large as of publication. Anyone with information can call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS or 888-57-PISTA for Spanish.

man-stabbed-in-abdomen-robbed-of-cellpho.title: Man Stabbed in Abdomen and Robbed of Cellphone in Flushing; Two Arrested
man-stabbed-in-abdomen-robbed-of-cellpho.dek: A 31-year-old man was stabbed and robbed of his phone near 37th Avenue in Flushing. Police arrested two people in connection with the robbery, Hoodline reported.
body: Oct. 1, early morning. A Flushing street. A 31-year-old man was stabbed multiple times in the abdomen and robbed of his cellphone, according to Hoodline.

It happened near 109-15 37th Avenue in Queens, Hoodline reported. Citing News 12, the outlet said the robbery took place shortly after 2 a.m. Another account cited in the article put it at about 2:10 a.m.

News 12's account, as cited by Hoodline, says four people approached the man. They showed a cutting instrument, stabbed him and took his phone. Hoodline noted that other accounts differed. One described a single attacker. Another said police were seeking three suspects. Those differences had not been resolved, the outlet said.
The man was taken to New York-Presbyterian Queens Hospital, according to News 12. His current condition was not reported.

Police arrested Mateo Tonato, 20, and Scarleth Remache, 19, in connection with the robbery, according to the report. Both face assault and robbery charges, News 12 reported. The charges are accusations. Both are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

man-shot-in-leg-in-car-near-bed-stuy-sch.title: Man Shot in Leg Near Bed-Stuy School; Students Shelter in Place
man-shot-in-leg-in-car-near-bed-stuy-sch.dek: A man sitting in a car at Monroe Street and Ralph Avenue was shot in the leg. A nearby school kept students inside as a precaution.
body: Tuesday, just after 1 p.m. Monroe Street and Ralph Avenue in Bedford-Stuyvesant. A man sitting in a car was shot in the leg, Hoodline reported, citing police via News12.
The man was taken to Wyckoff Hospital, according to Hoodline. His age and condition were not reported.

A school near P.S. 309, a few blocks away, went into shelter-in-place while police responded, Hoodline reported. Students and staff stayed inside as a precaution. No students were hurt. School staff said the order was lifted later the same day.

As of the latest reporting, police had not announced any arrests, according to Hoodline. They had not released a description of a suspect. The outlet attributed details of the shooting to police, through News12. It attributed the status of the school to school staff.
The shooting is still under investigation. Hoodline noted that a January shooting on Marcus Garvey Boulevard also led to a lockdown at a nearby Success Academy school, according to News12.

four-men-beat-driver-with-pipe-and-steal.title: Four Men Beat Driver With Pipe and Steal His SUV in East Williamsburg
four-men-beat-driver-with-pipe-and-steal.dek: Police released images of four men sought in an Oct. 6 carjacking outside 364 Ten Eyck Street.
body: Oct. 6, about 1 a.m. Outside 364 Ten Eyck Street in East Williamsburg. Four men beat a 27-year-old driver with a metal pipe and stole his SUV. Police are searching for them, Hoodline reported.
Citing News12 New York, Hoodline reported that the four men surrounded the man's blue 2026 Toyota Highlander. They forced him out. They punched him in the face. They struck him with the pipe.
The men took his car keys, his cellphone and a wallet with $200 in it, Hoodline reported. Then they drove off south on Morgan Street in the Highlander. The driver was treated at the scene.
Police released images of the four men, according to Hoodline. They wore dark hooded sweatshirts or jackets. The area is covered by the NYPD's 90th Precinct.
No arrests had been reported as of Hoodline's report. Investigators asked anyone with information to come forward or contact NYPD Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS.

canarsie-man-67-beaten-from-behind-and-r.title: Canarsie Man, 67, Beaten From Behind and Robbed of Phone and iPad
canarsie-man-67-beaten-from-behind-and-r.dek: An attacker punched and kicked a 67-year-old man near East 101st Street and Avenue J, then ran off with his devices, police said.
body: A Monday afternoon. Near East 101st Street and Avenue J in Canarsie. A 67-year-old man was beaten and robbed, Hoodline reported, citing police.

The attacker came up behind the man, according to Hoodline. He punched and kicked him again and again as the man tried to defend himself. The man suffered cuts and swelling to his face. He was taken to Mount Sinai Brooklyn for treatment.
The attacker ran off along East 101st Street with the man's cellphone and iPad, Hoodline reported, citing News12 Brooklyn.

Police have not released a description of the attacker, according to Hoodline. No arrest has been reported. The outlet noted earlier attacks on older men in the area. One was a February assault on an 80-year-old on Rockaway Parkway. No link to this case has been established, it said.
The investigation is ongoing, according to Hoodline. Anyone with information about the attack is asked to call NYPD Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS (8477).

man-wounded-in-daytime-shooting-near-bro.title: Man Wounded in Daytime Shooting on Bay Parkway in Bath Beach
man-wounded-in-daytime-shooting-near-bro.dek: A 32-year-old man was shot in the hand and leg outside a Bath Beach building on Oct. 14. Police were searching for the gunman, amNY reported.
body: Wednesday, Oct. 14, about 1:40 p.m. In front of 8817 Bay Parkway near Cropsey Avenue in Bath Beach, Brooklyn. A 32-year-old man was shot and wounded, according to police cited by amNY.
Officers from the 62nd Precinct responded after a 911 call, police said. They found the man with gunshot wounds to his left hand and left leg.
EMS took him to NYU Langone Hospital-Brooklyn. He was listed in stable condition, police sources told amNY.

Early in the investigation, police had not identified a motive. They had not released a description of the shooter. Detectives were canvassing the area for video cameras that may have recorded the shooting. No arrests had been made, according to the report.

The 62nd Precinct had recorded three shooting incidents this year through Oct. 11, according to NYPD statistics cited by amNY. That is one more than at the same point in 2025. Police asked anyone with information to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

man-stabbed-after-argument-on-6-train-ne.title: Man Stabbed After Argument on Uptown 6 Train Near Astor Place
man-stabbed-after-argument-on-6-train-ne.dek: A 40-year-old man was stabbed multiple times after a dispute aboard a 6 train in the East Village. Police were looking for a masked suspect, amNY reported.
body: Wednesday, Oct. 14, about 2:25 a.m. An uptown 6 train near the Astor Place station in the East Village. A 40-year-old man was stabbed multiple times, according to police sources cited by amNY.
Officers from the 9th Precinct and NYPD Transit District 4 were alerted, the outlet reported. They found the wounded man after the train pulled into Astor Place.
EMS took the man to Bellevue Hospital. He was listed in stable condition, according to the report.
A preliminary investigation found the man had a verbal dispute with the suspect before the stabbing, police said. What the argument was about is not known.

The suspect fled the station. Police described him as a man with a dark complexion wearing a ski mask. No arrests had been made. The investigation was continuing, according to amNY. Police asked anyone with information to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

24-year-old-stabbed-on-2-train-platform-.title: Man, 24, Stabbed on 2 Train Platform at East 180th Street Station
24-year-old-stabbed-on-2-train-platform-.dek: A 24-year-old man was stabbed Tuesday night on the northbound 2 train platform at the East 180th Street station in the Bronx. No arrests had been made, Hoodline reported.
body: Tuesday, Oct. 13, night. The northbound 2 train platform at the East 180th Street station in the Bronx. A 24-year-old man was stabbed, police said, according to Hoodline.
The man was taken to a local hospital in stable condition, police said. PIX11, citing sources, reported that he had been uncooperative with investigators, according to Hoodline.
Detectives were searching for a suspect. No arrests had been made as of Wednesday, the outlet reported. Police had not released a description of the attacker. They had not announced any charges.

Hoodline noted several earlier incidents at the same station this year. In late July, a 45-year-old man was slashed in the neck after an argument on the northbound platform, according to reports cited by the outlet. On Aug. 17, a 31-year-old commuter was slashed in the arm aboard a southbound 2 train. In late August, a 65-year-old woman was pushed onto the tracks from the 5 train platform. Police rescued her and took a person of interest into custody, News 12 Bronx reported.

NYPD CompStat figures through Oct. 11 showed subway transit crime complaints up 1.6% year to date, according to Hoodline. The outlet noted that no count for this station was available. Police asked anyone with information to call Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS.

teen-15-slashed-in-head-during-melee-in-.title: Teen, 15, Slashed in Head During Melee in Flushing Meadows Corona Park
teen-15-slashed-in-head-during-melee-in-.dek: Police answering a shots-fired call near the New York Hall of Science on Oct. 12 found a large group and a 15-year-old boy with slash wounds, QNS reported.
body: Monday, Oct. 12, afternoon. Inside Flushing Meadows Corona Park. A 15-year-old boy was slashed across the head and left arm during a melee involving a large, disorderly group, according to the NYPD as cited by QNS.

Just after 5 p.m., officers from the 110th Precinct were sent to reports of shots fired near 111th Street and 47th Avenue in Corona, the outlet reported. That is close to the New York Hall of Science. They found the group in the park. Then they learned the teenager had been hurt.
EMS took the boy to Harlem Hospital. He was listed in stable condition, police said. According to police, EMS chose Harlem Hospital over Elmhurst Hospital, which is about two miles away.
Police said they were looking for two people: a gunman, and a separate person who did the slashing. No arrests had been made. The investigation was continuing, according to QNS.

Through Oct. 11, the 110th Precinct had reported 550 felony assaults this year, according to CompStat figures cited by the outlet. That is up 15.1% from 478 at the same point last year. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

bronx-vigil-honors-young-mother-allegedl.title: Bronx Vigil Honors Young Mother Allegedly Pushed From Balcony
bronx-vigil-honors-young-mother-allegedl.dek: Community members and advocates gathered a week after investigators say a 23-year-old woman and her infant were pushed from a 15th-floor balcony by her ex-boyfriend.
body: Tuesday night, in the Bronx. Community members and advocates held a candlelight vigil for a 23-year-old mother, NY1 reported. Investigators say her ex-boyfriend pushed her from a high-rise balcony a week earlier.

Investigators said the man pushed the woman and the couple's 8-month-old daughter off a 15th-floor balcony at a Bronx building, according to NY1. Officials said the woman was holding the child when she fell. Officials said the infant was still hospitalized in critical condition.

The ex-boyfriend, Angel Carrasco, faces several charges, including murder and attempted murder. Police sources told NY1 he had been taken to a hospital. He had not yet been arraigned. He is presumed innocent.

Bronx Borough President Vanessa Gibson said the woman's mother and grandmother were at the hospital with the baby. She said the community takes the attack personally. Council Member Kevin Riley urged men to do more to stop violence against women and children.

Advocates said they hope the case raises awareness of domestic violence, including warning signs and how to seek help. Stephanie McGraw founded the domestic violence organization WARM. She said neighbors should speak up when they hear yelling, screaming or breaking glass. October is Domestic Violence Awareness Month. Advocates have been canvassing the area to share information about resources for victims, NY1 reported.

off-duty-nypd-detective-who-was-stabbed-.title: Off-Duty NYPD Detective Stabbed and Robbed in Norwood Speaks Publicly
off-duty-nypd-detective-who-was-stabbed-.dek: The detective, attacked Oct. 2 in the Bronx while on vacation, described identifying himself as an officer and chasing his attackers.
body: Oct. 2. The Bronx's Norwood neighborhood. An off-duty NYPD detective was stabbed and robbed. On Tuesday he spoke to reporters for the first time since, News 12 Bronx reported.

He said he was stabbed 10 times, according to News 12. Stitches were visible on his right arm. His left arm was in a cast. He said he needs surgery and is working to regain movement in his left hand. He had been on vacation at the time.

He said he told the attackers in English and Spanish that he was a police officer. He said they ignored him. Despite his injuries, he said, he chased them for about five blocks. Then he asked a passerby for help, and that person called 911. He told News 12 his police training made his response instinctive. He said his main goal was to give responders a clear description of the suspects.

Two men, Dangelo Caraballo and Sneider Mejia, were arrested in Massachusetts, News 12 reported. They were brought back to the Bronx on Tuesday to await arraignment. Both live about half a mile from where the attack took place. They face charges including attempted murder, robbery and assault on a police officer. They are presumed innocent.

nearby-shooting-puts-bed-stuy-school-in-.title: Shooting Near Bed-Stuy School Prompts Shelter-in-Place
nearby-shooting-puts-bed-stuy-school-in-.dek: A person sitting in a car was shot in the leg at Monroe Street and Ralph Avenue. A nearby school sheltered in place, News 12 Brooklyn reported.
body: Tuesday, Oct. 13. A shooting in Bedford-Stuyvesant. A school nearby was placed under a shelter-in-place, News 12 Brooklyn reported.

Police said the shooting happened just after 1 p.m. at Monroe Street and Ralph Avenue, near P.S. 309, according to the outlet. The victim was sitting inside a car. The victim was shot in the right leg, News 12 reported. The article did not say exactly which school was placed under the order. It did not say when the order began.
The victim was taken to Wyckoff Hospital for treatment. The report did not describe the person's condition. It did not give the victim's name, age or gender.
School staff told News 12 that the shelter-in-place was lifted later in the day. They said no students were hurt.
No arrests had been made at the time of the report, according to police. News 12 did not report a description of a suspect. It did not report a possible motive. The investigation was continuing.

12-year-old-girl-shot-near-westchester-s.title: 12-Year-Old Girl Wounded in Bronx Shooting; Two Men Sought
12-year-old-girl-shot-near-westchester-s.dek: A 12-year-old girl was shot in the torso and foot on Tratman Avenue in the Bronx on Monday night. Police were looking for two men, News 12 Bronx reported.
body: Monday, Oct. 12, about 8:30 p.m. Outside 2465 Tratman Avenue near Rowland Street in the Bronx. A 12-year-old girl was shot in the torso and right foot, according to News 12 Bronx.
Police sources told News 12 the girl was not the intended target. It was not immediately clear who was.

The girl was taken to Montefiore Hospital by private means. She was in stable condition, police said. The FDNY said she had already left the scene when its emergency medical crews arrived, according to the report.
Video from the scene showed a gun lying on the street beside a car tire, News 12 reported. About seven evidence markers for shell casings were visible as investigators collected evidence.

Police sources said two men dressed in all black ran toward Zerega Avenue after the shooting. No arrests had been made at the time of the report. Police were still investigating what led to the gunfire.

flushing-man-charged-with-manslaughter-i.title: Flushing Man Charged With Manslaughter in Crash That Killed Baby in Stroller
flushing-man-charged-with-manslaughter-i.dek: Queens prosecutors say a 57-year-old driver was impaired by drugs when he ran a stop sign in Murray Hill and hit a stroller carrying a 1-year-old boy, QNS reported.
body: A 57-year-old Flushing man has been charged with manslaughter, according to QNS. Prosecutors say he struck and killed a 1-year-old boy in a stroller while driving under the influence of drugs in Murray Hill, Queens.

Sunday, Oct. 11, about 8:35 a.m. Prosecutors identified the driver as Elvin Rivera of 150th Place. According to the charges, Rivera was driving a white 2016 Chevrolet Silverado north on Murray Street, the outlet reported. He rolled through the stop sign at 32nd Avenue. He accelerated. He hit the stroller in a marked crosswalk.

The boy's 69-year-old nanny was pushing the stroller about three blocks from the child's home, according to the report. EMS took the boy to Jacobi Hospital in critical condition. He was later pronounced dead there. The nanny was taken to NewYork-Presbyterian Queens Hospital in stable condition with an arm injury.

Rivera stayed at the scene. Officers from the 109th Precinct took him into custody, QNS reported. Prosecutors said he failed a field sobriety test. They said a roadside drug test detected cocaine and THC. The outlet noted he has an open DWI case in the Bronx from April.

He was arraigned Oct. 12 on charges including second-degree manslaughter, vehicular manslaughter and driving under the influence, according to the report. He pleaded not guilty. He was ordered held without bail. He is due back in court Oct. 19. Queens District Attorney Melinda Katz called the death completely avoidable. Rivera is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

videos-show-marble-hill-ice-shooting-unf.title: Videos Show Marble Hill ICE Shooting Unfolded in Seconds
videos-show-marble-hill-ice-shooting-unf.dek: Footage of the Oct. 8 shooting in Marble Hill shows a brief, chaotic encounter. Federal officials say officers believed they were in danger.
body: Oct. 8. Marble Hill. Video of the shooting by immigration officers shows the encounter unfolded in a few chaotic seconds, according to an Associated Press report published by NY1. A 28-year-old Dominican man was driving with his 5-year-old son. The man was wounded. The child was not hurt.

One NYPD camera video shows two plainclothes officers running to the car with guns drawn, the AP reported. One strikes a window with his gun. The driver speeds away. A second video shows people diving for cover as the car stops against a concrete barrier. There are bullet holes in the windshield and a rear window. The footage did not show whether the shooting was justified.

Marcos Charles heads ICE enforcement and removal operations. He said the driver refused orders, accelerated and hit two government vehicles, and that officers believed their lives were in danger. He called the neck wound superficial. Senior officials said officers did not know the child was in the car. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin blamed the driver for putting his son at risk.

Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said federal officers fired seven rounds, according to the AP. Mayor Zohran Mamdani called the shooting an outrage. He and Gov. Kathy Hochul said they pressed Mullin and President Trump for the man's release without success. They urged release of ICE body camera footage. Mullin said the footage would be released. He did not say when.

The man's lawyers say he is held in a federal jail in Brooklyn with a bullet still in his body. A judge temporarily barred the government from removing him. Bronx District Attorney Darcel Clark said her office is investigating.

marble-hill-detainee-still-has-bullet-in.title: Marble Hill Detainee Still Has Bullet in His Neck, Attorneys Say
marble-hill-detainee-still-has-bullet-in.dek: Lawyers for the man shot by an ICE agent in Marble Hill say he is still in federal custody in Brooklyn without needed surgery.
body: Oct. 8, Marble Hill. A man was shot by an ICE agent. His attorneys from the Legal Aid Society and Make the Road New York say he still has a bullet lodged in his neck, according to amNY. They say he has not eaten since being taken into custody.

He is held at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Sunset Park, Brooklyn, the attorneys said. They described harsh conditions, reportedly solitary confinement. They said he has had only water from a bathroom sink, amNY reported. After the shooting he was taken from NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital in an ICE vehicle. Police pushed back protesters.

His lawyers say he has numbness on the left side of his face, hearing problems in his left ear and a shoulder wound from broken glass. Doctors said he urgently needs surgery, amNY reported. They considered it too dangerous without a specialized surgeon. It is unclear whether it will happen.

The attorneys accused ICE of deliberate indifference and due process violations. They filed a habeas corpus petition. It prevents his immediate deportation or removal from New York. The Department of Homeland Security maintains that he is a criminal and a member of the Trinitarios gang, according to amNY.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani spoke on MS NOW on Sunday. He compared the chaos on the street to a mass shooting. As of the report, the man was still in detention, awaiting legal proceedings.

rider-slashed-during-argument-on-4-train.title: Rider Slashed in Face During Argument on 4 Train Near Grand Central
rider-slashed-during-argument-on-4-train.dek: Police released images of a man they say slashed a 34-year-old rider across the face aboard a downtown 4 train on Oct. 8, amNY reported.
body: Oct. 8, about 9:25 p.m. A downtown 4 train approaching the 42nd Street-Grand Central station. A 34-year-old rider was slashed across the face. Police are searching for the man they say did it, according to amNY.
The preliminary police account cited by the outlet says the two men got into a verbal dispute. It turned into a physical struggle. The suspect pulled out a sharp object and cut the victim.
The incident was reported to the Midtown South Precinct. Officers from NYPD Transit District 4 responded. EMS took the injured man to Bellevue Hospital in stable condition, according to the report.

The suspect fled in an unknown direction, police said. Investigators released images of him on Sunday night, Oct. 11. They said he was last seen wearing a black jacket, blue jeans and multicolored sneakers.
No arrests had been reported. Police asked anyone with information to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS or submit tips at crimestoppers.nypdonline.org, according to amNY.

teen-arrested-in-armed-flushing-home-inv.title: Teen Arrested in Armed Flushing Home Invasion; Three Others Sought
teen-arrested-in-armed-flushing-home-inv.dek: Police arrested a 17-year-old after four masked men forced their way into a Flushing home and robbed a 45-year-old man, QNS reported.
body: Sunday, Oct. 11, about 2:30 a.m. A residence on the Horace Harding Expressway near 150th Street in Flushing. Four masked men forced their way in, police said, according to QNS. A 17-year-old has been arrested. Three other men are still at large.
Three of the men displayed firearms and demanded the 45-year-old resident's property, police said. The fourth struck him in the face with a crowbar. He was left with cuts to his face.

The intruders took the man's watch and a chain, the outlet reported. Police valued them at about $65,000. The men left him zip-tied and fled in an unknown direction. He declined medical attention at the scene.

Officers from the 109th Precinct arrested the 17-year-old nearby a short time later, police said. He was charged with robbery, assault, burglary, grand larceny, criminal trespass and harassment, according to QNS. His arraignment in Queens Criminal Court was pending. The charges are accusations. He is presumed innocent.
Police asked anyone with information about the three remaining suspects to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

queens-man-charged-in-fatal-beating-at-c.title: Queens Man Charged With Murder in Fatal Beating Outside Chelsea Adult Store
queens-man-charged-in-fatal-beating-at-c.dek: Police charged a 25-year-old Queens man with murder and robbery after a 60-year-old Pennsylvania man was beaten to death following an argument in a Chelsea store, amNY reported.
body: A 60-year-old Pennsylvania man is dead. A 25-year-old Queens man has been charged with murder and two counts of robbery, according to amNY. The man was beaten after an argument inside a Chelsea adult store on Sunday night.
Police identified the accused as Imani McColley. His last known address was a homeless shelter in Jamaica, Queens, the outlet reported.

Sunday, about 9 p.m. Rainbow Station, an adult store at 203 Eighth Avenue. The confrontation began inside, police said. The argument turned physical and spilled onto the street. There, police said, McColley allegedly shoved the man to the ground, stomped on him repeatedly, took his wallet and fled.

A 911 call reported an assault in progress. Officers from the 10th Precinct and paramedics responded and found the man badly hurt. EMS took him to Bellevue Hospital. He was pronounced dead there, according to the report.

Police sources told amNY that McColley came back to the scene later that night. An eyewitness pointed him out to officers. They took him into custody. The killing appeared to be the 10th Precinct's first murder of the year, according to NYPD statistics cited by the outlet.
The charges are accusations. McColley is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. The article did not report a court appearance or plea.

wrong-way-crash-on-west-shore-expressway.title: Wrong-Way Crash on Staten Island's West Shore Expressway Kills One, Injures Four
wrong-way-crash-on-west-shore-expressway.dek: A 66-year-old driver died after her car struck a Range Rover traveling the wrong way on the West Shore Expressway, police said.
body: Saturday morning. Staten Island's West Shore Expressway. A wrong-way driver set off a three-car crash. One person was killed. Four others were hospitalized, police said, according to Hoodline.

A Range Rover heading north ended up in the southbound lanes, according to the report. A southbound Kia Seltos driven by a 66-year-old woman struck it. A southbound Jeep driven by a 21-year-old woman then hit both vehicles.

The 66-year-old Kia driver was pronounced dead at the scene. Four people were taken to Richmond University Medical Center: the Jeep driver, the 36-year-old woman driving the Range Rover and two passengers in the Jeep. They were listed in stable condition, Hoodline reported, citing ABC7.
All of the drivers stayed at the scene. The NYPD Collision Investigation Squad is investigating. No arrests have been made. Police have not announced a cause.

Wrong-way crashes caused 704 deaths nationwide in 2022, up from 445 in 2018, Hoodline noted, citing Federal Highway Administration figures. The same expressway was the site of a fatal wrong-way crash in 2015.

one-dead-one-hurt-in-park-hill-avenue-fi.title: One Dead, One Injured in Park Hill Avenue Apartment Fire on Staten Island
one-dead-one-hurt-in-park-hill-avenue-fi.dek: A Saturday-night fire in a six-story apartment building on Park Hill Avenue killed one person and injured another, the FDNY said.
body: Saturday night. A six-story apartment building on Park Hill Avenue on Staten Island. Fire broke out. One person was killed and another was injured, according to the FDNY, Hoodline reported.

The fire was reported at about 8:08 p.m. on the building's second floor, according to the report. The building is on the stretch of Park Hill Avenue between Sobel Court and Roff Street. The injured person was evaluated at the scene. Their condition was not known as of Saturday night, CBS News New York reported. The person who died had not been publicly identified.
No cause has been made public, according to Hoodline.

The block has had several fires in recent years. In June, a fire on the fourth floor of a building at 140 Park Hill Ave. injured a civilian and seriously injured a firefighter, according to the Staten Island Advance. In May 2021, a fifth-floor fire a few doors from Saturday's scene injured a civilian and a police officer, according to NY Fire News.

The building is part of the federally subsidized Park Hill Apartments complex. A joint venture of The Arker Companies, L+M Development Partners and LIHC Investment Group bought it in December 2025 for $364.7 million, Hoodline previously reported. The sale followed nearly 2,000 resident complaints to the city over heat and hot water outages. It was described as a recapitalization to fund repairs.
Citywide, 46 people died in fires from January through mid-May, an FDNY official told CBS News. That was up from 28 in the same period of 2025.

mamdani-says-ice-agent-looked-like-a-mas.title: Mamdani Says ICE Agent Looked Like a Mass Shooter at Marble Hill Stop
mamdani-says-ice-agent-looked-like-a-mas.dek: The mayor criticized the federal agent who opened fire during an Oct. 8 traffic stop in Marble Hill as footage of the encounter came out.
body: Oct. 8. A traffic stop in Marble Hill. An ICE agent shot a 28-year-old driver. The man's 5-year-old child was in the car. On Sunday, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the agent looked like a mass shooter, amNY reported.

NYPD body camera footage shows officers arriving to find an ICE agent in a construction vest holding a long gun, according to amNY. Surveillance video shows an agent rushing toward the man's Honda with a gun displayed. It does not clearly show whether he identified himself as a federal officer. The driver pulled away as shots were fired. Pedestrians ducked for cover.

Mamdani spoke on MS NOW's Connect with Jacob Soboroff. He said ICE treats the law as optional and that bystanders were unsure what they were seeing, amNY reported. He has said he tried to negotiate the man's release with President Trump. They did not reach an agreement.

amNY reported that the same agent was seen during an October 2025 federal raid on Canal Street, detaining immigrants at court hearings and in Minneapolis. The Department of Homeland Security says the wounded man is associated with the Trinitarios gang. The FBI is investigating the shooting, according to amNY.

Protests followed. Darializa Avila Chevalier, the Democratic nominee for Congress, was pushed to the ground during clashes with police. She called on Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch to resign. Sources told amNY that Tisch has no plans to step down. Mamdani does not intend to ask her to.

robber-assaults-19-year-old-worker-at-br.title: Robber Assaults 19-Year-Old Worker at Staten Island's Bricktown Centre
robber-assaults-19-year-old-worker-at-br.dek: Police are asking for help identifying a shoplifting suspect who attacked an employee who confronted them at a store on Bricktown Way.
body: A Sunday, about 6:10 p.m. A store at 165 Bricktown Way, at Bricktown Centre at Charleston on Staten Island. A shoplifting suspect attacked a 19-year-old employee, Hoodline reported, citing NYPD Crime Stoppers. Police are asking the public for help identifying the suspect.

Police said the suspect took merchandise and walked past all points of sale without paying, according to Hoodline. The employee confronted the suspect. The suspect attacked her. Hoodline reported that the attack included a sexual assault.

Accounts of the weapon differ. The article's text said the suspect struck the worker with what it described as a firearm. The page's summary said she was pepper-sprayed. Hoodline did not reconcile the two.
Police have not released a description of the suspect. Hoodline quoted no police officials directly.

No arrests had been announced as of the Crime Stoppers alert. The suspect is still at large, according to Hoodline. A reward of up to $3,500 is offered for information leading to an arrest and felony indictment. Tips can be shared with Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS.

pedestrian-fighting-for-his-life-after-q.title: Pedestrian Critically Injured in Jamaica Avenue Hit-and-Run
pedestrian-fighting-for-his-life-after-q.dek: A 54-year-old man was struck by a driver who fled on Jamaica Avenue near 184th Street early Sunday, amNY reported.
body: Sunday, Oct. 11, about 1:51 a.m. Jamaica Avenue near 184th Street in Queens. A driver struck a 54-year-old man and fled. The man was critically injured, according to police sources cited by amNY.
Police said the man was crossing Jamaica Avenue from the northwest corner to the southwest corner. An eastbound gray Ford Crown Victoria hit him.
The man suffered serious head and body injuries, police said. EMS took him to Jamaica Hospital Medical Center. He was listed in critical condition, according to the report.
The driver did not stay at the scene, police said. The car kept going east on Jamaica Avenue. No arrests had been made at the time of publication.

The NYPD Highway District Investigation Squad is leading the investigation, amNY reported. Police asked anyone with information to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS, submit tips at crimestoppers.nypdonline.org or message @NYPDTips on X.

two-slashed-on-beach-54th-street-suspect.title: Man Arrested After Two Slashed, Standoff at Far Rockaway Building
two-slashed-on-beach-54th-street-suspect.dek: Police said a 52-year-old man slashed a man and a woman at a Beach 54th Street apartment building and then barricaded himself inside, ABC7 New York reported.
body: Just before midnight. An apartment building on Beach 54th Street in Far Rockaway, Queens. Police said a 52-year-old man slashed two people there and then barricaded himself inside, according to ABC7 New York. He was taken into custody.
The station's article was published Saturday, Oct. 10. It did not give the calendar date of the incident.
A man and a woman were injured in the slashing, according to authorities cited by ABC7. Both were expected to recover.

Officers responded to the building, police said. The suspect had barricaded himself inside after the attack. During the response, one officer fired a weapon. No one was struck, authorities said. The article did not say what led the officer to fire.

Police said the suspect was eventually taken into custody. His name was not released. The station reported nothing about charges, bail or a court date. The victims were not identified. Authorities said more details were not immediately available. The suspect is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

stapleton-man-accused-of-booting-neighbo.title: Stapleton Man Charged After Allegedly Booting Car Blocking His Driveway
stapleton-man-accused-of-booting-neighbo.dek: Police say a Staten Island man put a wheel boot on a Jeep parked across his Waverly Place driveway and demanded $25, then was found carrying a stun gun, Hoodline reported.
body: A 52-year-old Stapleton man has been charged, according to Hoodline. Police say he put a wheel boot on a car blocking his driveway on Waverly Place. They say he left a note demanding $25 to remove it.

Oct. 2, near Targee Street. The man, identified as Aaron Hardy, allegedly attached the boot to the front left tire of a gray 2015 Jeep Compass, according to a criminal complaint cited by silive.com. The driver had parked at about 7:30 a.m. The driver found the boot around 3 p.m., the reports said.

Hardy told police he had paperwork authorizing him to boot the car, according to the reports. He said 311 had told him he could. Gothamist reported that the city has no provision letting residents boot other people's cars without a license. Police said Hardy removed the boot himself with a key. When officers arrested him, they found an electronic stun gun in his waistband.

He faces charges including felony criminal possession of a weapon, third-degree coercion, attempted petit larceny and criminal tampering, according to silive.com and Gothamist. Hardy pleaded not guilty. He was released on non-monetary conditions.

His attorney, Kelvin Richards, said Hardy is innocent and will fight the charges, the reports said. Richards also acknowledged that Hardy booted the car. He said the driver had interfered with Hardy's car wash and repair business. Hardy is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

mamdani-says-talks-with-trump-failed-to-.title: Mamdani Says Talks With Trump Failed to Free Man Shot by ICE Agents
mamdani-says-talks-with-trump-failed-to-.dek: Federal agents removed the wounded man from a Manhattan hospital after the mayor's appeals to President Trump and DHS did not succeed.
body: Thursday night. Mayor Zohran Mamdani said talks with President Trump and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin had failed to win the release of a 28-year-old man shot by federal immigration agents in Marble Hill, amNY reported. Mamdani said agents then removed the man from NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital in an unmarked vehicle.

Oct. 8, shortly after 4 p.m. Near 2 Marble Hill Ave. Agents were trying to take the man into custody, according to amNY. Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said at least one ICE agent fired seven rounds. One struck the driver in the neck. A 5-year-old boy in the vehicle was unharmed. He is with a family member.

Surveillance video showed a plainclothes officer approaching the driver's window with a drawn gun, amNY reported. Then the vehicle moved out of view. The cameras did not capture the shooting. NYPD officers responding to an unrelated call found the man handcuffed on the ground. They took him to the hospital in stable condition. Tisch said the NYPD had no involvement in the federal operation.

The Department of Homeland Security said officers were conducting a targeted arrest of a Dominican national with a prior grand larceny conviction and claimed gang ties. amNY said it had not verified that. DHS did not say what prompted the shots. It did not say whether the man was armed.

Mamdani called the shooting an outrage. He renewed his call to abolish ICE. Gov. Kathy Hochul said she urged Trump and Mullin to halt enforcement in New York and release body camera footage. Federal agents have taken control of the investigation.

teen-stabbed-and-beaten-with-bat-near-br.title: Teen Stabbed and Beaten With Bat Near Crown Heights School; Five Sought
teen-stabbed-and-beaten-with-bat-near-br.dek: A 16-year-old boy was stabbed and struck with a bat on President Street in Crown Heights. Police were searching for five suspects, amNY reported.
body: Friday, Oct. 9, just before 10 a.m. In front of an apartment building at 993 President Street in Crown Heights, Brooklyn. A 16-year-old boy was stabbed and beaten with a bat, according to police cited by amNY.

Police said five males confronted the teen. A verbal dispute followed. When he tried to run away, the attack escalated, police said. Law enforcement sources told amNY that one suspect stabbed the teen in the back. Another struck his legs and knees several times with a bat.

The teen ran about a block to the Prospect Heights High School Campus on Classon Avenue, sources said. School Safety Agents helped him and called police. Officers from the 71st Precinct responded to the school.
EMS took the boy to Maimonides Medical Center. He was listed in stable condition, the outlet reported.

The suspects were last seen running west on President Street. No arrests had been made. The investigation was continuing, police said. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

queens-man-charged-with-sex-abuse-of-gir.title: Ozone Park Man Charged With Sex Abuse of Girl; Police Seek Other Victims
queens-man-charged-with-sex-abuse-of-gir.dek: A 72-year-old Queens man was arrested on sex abuse charges involving a 12-year-old girl. Detectives said he may have other victims, amNY reported.
body: A 72-year-old Ozone Park man has been charged with sexually abusing a 12-year-old girl, according to amNY. Police said they believe he may have attacked others.

Police identified the accused as Nazim Uddin of 75th Street. Sept. 8, about 7 p.m. A commercial establishment near 75th Street and 101st Avenue, not far from his home. That is where the alleged abuse took place, according to police sources. The article did not say whether he worked at the business. It did not say what connection, if any, he had to the girl.
The Queens Child Abuse Squad arrested Uddin on the afternoon of Oct. 8, about a month later, the outlet reported. He was booked on charges of sexual abuse and acting in a manner injurious to a child.

Special victims detectives believe there may be more victims, based on a preliminary investigation, police said. The NYPD issued an alert Thursday night. It asks anyone who may have been harmed by him to come forward.

Court records showed Uddin was scheduled for arraignment in Queens Criminal Court on Friday, Oct. 9, amNY reported. The outcome was not reported. The charges are accusations. He is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. Police asked anyone with information to call the NYPD Sex Crimes Hotline at 212-267-7273 or Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

teen-shot-dead-at-harlem-public-housing-.title: Teen Fatally Shot at Harlem Housing Complex; Person of Interest Questioned
teen-shot-dead-at-harlem-public-housing-.dek: A 15-year-old boy was killed and a 57-year-old bystander wounded in a shooting at King Towers in Harlem. Detectives were questioning a person of interest, amNY reported.
body: Wednesday, Oct. 7, just after 6:20 p.m. The King Towers public housing complex at 40 West 115th Street in Harlem. A 15-year-old boy was fatally shot. A 57-year-old man was wounded, according to the NYPD as cited by amNY.

Officers from the 28th Precinct and NYPD Public Service Area 5 responded after a ShotSpotter activation, police said. They found the teenager, a resident of King Towers, with a gunshot wound to the stomach. EMS took him to Mount Sinai Morningside Hospital in critical condition. He died a short time later.

The 57-year-old man was struck in the right hand, police said. Investigators determined he was a bystander hit by a stray bullet. He was taken to Harlem Hospital in stable condition, according to the report.

Police took a person of interest into custody during the preliminary investigation, amNY reported. Charges were pending the outcome of the inquiry. As of Thursday morning, the motive was unknown. Sources said detectives were looking into whether the teen was the intended target.
Through Oct. 4, the 28th Precinct had recorded three homicides this year, according to NYPD statistics cited by the outlet. A year earlier, it was five.

victim-identified-in-fatal-mount-eden-st.title: Police Identify Man Killed in Mount Eden Stabbing, Release Suspect Image
victim-identified-in-fatal-mount-eden-st.dek: A 27-year-old man died after being stabbed inside a Grand Concourse building in Mount Eden. Police released an image of a man they want to question, News 12 Bronx reported.
body: Wednesday, just after 1:50 p.m. Inside a building at 1555 Grand Concourse in the Mount Eden section of the Bronx. A 27-year-old man was fatally stabbed. Police have identified him, according to News 12 Bronx.
Investigators said the man suffered stab wounds to his neck, the outlet reported. He was taken to Lincoln Hospital. He died of his injuries there.

Police released a new image of a man they want in connection with the killing, News 12 reported. He was last seen wearing a gray sweatshirt, a black jacket, black and red pants, and gray and white sneakers. Police did not identify him.
No arrests had been reported. The investigation was still active, according to the outlet. The report did not describe a motive. It did not say whether the two men knew each other.
Police asked anyone with information about the stabbing or the man in the image to contact them. Tips can be submitted to NYPD Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

federal-immigration-agents-shoot-and-wou.title: Federal Immigration Agents Shoot and Wound Man in Marble Hill
federal-immigration-agents-shoot-and-wou.dek: Federal agents shot and injured a man during an attempted arrest at West 225th Street and Marble Hill Avenue, drawing protests and demands for answers from city and state officials, amNY reported.
body: Thursday, Oct. 8, about 4 p.m. West 225th Street and Marble Hill Avenue in the Bronx. Federal agents shot and wounded a man, according to law enforcement sources cited by amNY. Multiple outlets identified the agents as ICE officers. PIX11 reported the shooting likely happened during an attempted arrest.

The NYPD said the shooting involved federal agents. It said city police were not involved or on scene at the time. A 5-year-old child was in the back seat of the man's car and was not hurt, ABC7 reported. Mayor Zohran Mamdani confirmed that. The man, whose name was not released, was being treated at NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital.

Hours later, the Department of Homeland Security said agents were arresting a man from the Dominican Republic with a prior grand larceny conviction, amNY reported. It said ICE officers rendered aid. DHS did not explain why an agent fired. Sources told the outlet that NYPD officers drove the man to the hospital.

Mamdani called the shooting unconscionable. He said he called President Trump to demand an end to ICE enforcement in the city. Gov. Kathy Hochul said she spoke with Trump and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and demanded the release of body camera footage, according to the report. U.S. Rep. Adriano Espaillat said agents denied him access to the man at the hospital.

Residents gathered at the scene. Protesters later assembled outside Allen Hospital, where clashes broke out with NYPD officers, amNY reported. The New York Immigration Coalition called for an independent investigation led by the state attorney general.

bronx-man-accused-of-stabbing-homeless-m.title: Bronx Man Charged With Murder in Stabbing Death in Jamaica Park
bronx-man-accused-of-stabbing-homeless-m.dek: Police charged a 53-year-old Bronx man with murder after a homeless man was fatally stabbed in Major Mark Park in Jamaica, Queens, QNS reported.
body: Wednesday, Oct. 7, morning. Major Mark Park in Jamaica, Queens. A homeless man was fatally stabbed. A 53-year-old Bronx man has been charged with murder, according to the NYPD as cited by QNS.

At 4:45 a.m., officers from the 103rd Precinct responded to a 911 call reporting an assault in progress inside the park, police said. The park is across from an apartment building at 87-70 173rd Street. They found a man with two stab wounds to the chest. EMS pronounced him dead at the scene. Investigators believe he was in his 30s. His name was withheld pending family notification.

Police canvassed the area with a witness, according to a law enforcement source cited by the outlet. The witness recognized a man walking several blocks away. He was first detained as a person of interest.

Police identified him as Abdullah Spencerel of Ogden Avenue in Highbridge. He was formally arrested nearly eight hours later, QNS reported. Several witnesses said they saw him arguing with the victim before the stabbing. He was charged with murder and criminal possession of a weapon.

An NYPD spokesman could not say what the argument was about. Spencerel was expected to be arraigned in Queens Criminal Court on Thursday, according to the report. The charges are accusations. He is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.
